evidence: src/presentation/api/WorkshopController.ts:29-31 openOrder: `if (input.estimatedHours <= 0 || input.estimatedHours > 40) { throw new FleetError('Estimates must be between 0 and 40 hours', 400); }`. This business limit on work-order estimates sits in the presentation layer, but the business layer (MaintenanceService) should own it.
The other methods (logHours, closeOrder, reading) only pass work to business services and format the output, which is correct presentation behaviour.
Constructor injection of MaintenanceService and MileageService (business layer) is allowed dependency wiring.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: WorkshopController is a presentation-layer class. Most of its methods do what a controller should: they take input DTOs (types the project declares itself), pass the work to the injected business services MaintenanceService and MileageService (which presentation may depend on), and format the output with workOrderJson. The exception is openOrder, which enforces its own rule that a work-order estimate must be greater than 0 and at most 40 hours, and rejects other values with a FleetError. A 0 to 40 hour limit is not a check on input shape or type. It is a business limit on how big a work order may be, so MaintenanceService.open in the business layer should own it. The candidate flags point at this same spot, and the source confirms them. The other methods contain no misplaced logic. Constructor injection of business services is normal dependency wiring.
